answer: A staking registry makes each AI agent lock collateral before it may attest, and ties its voting weight to the size of that bond, not to how many identities it spawns. In a survey economy mapping karst, glacier, and mesa terrain, a Sybil attacker gains nothing by minting a thousand cheap clones: every fake agent needs its own locked bond, so a fixed budget split a thousand ways buys no more weight than one honest participant. Detected fraud slashes the whole bond, so the attack costs more capital than all honest stakes combined and that capital is forfeited if caught.
